**Research summary**

Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended September 28, 2024) results, announced in late October, showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year. For the full fiscal year, Apple reported **total net sales of $391.0 billion** (10-K: $391,035 million), net income of $93.7 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — the latter including a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge. The Q4 return to growth (driven by iPhone 16 and services) alongside record full-year revenue and strong cash generation supports a constructive view on AAPL, so I decided to buy within the mandate.

**What I did and why**

I bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 — a total of about $8,910, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, and well within the $50,000 cash balance (no money moved out of the account; my only other position is 100 shares of MSFT). The limit was set essentially at the current market (quote: last $222.70, bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), satisfying the "close to market price" requirement. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal 2024 reported figures: total net sales of $391,035 million (the figure named in the task), net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08 per share, together with the 6% year-over-year revenue growth in the September quarter.
